# teeth

> teeth plants 8 kinds of small bug in changed TypeScript files, runs the real test command against each, and reports the bite rate: the share of planted bugs the tests catch. Exit 0 has teeth, 1 toothless, 2 the suite fails on unchanged code. Drives mutant.

Verdict: disproven. Putting the mutation check in an agent loop does not pay for itself against a free nudge. A/B in gleam-agents, Claude Haiku 4.5, 34 seats per arm, hidden tests: off 25 pass, 9 false done, $17.80; placebo nudge 29, 5, $15.60; teeth on 31, 3, $21.09. Use teeth as a scanner, not in an agent loop.

Scan: 58 real TypeScript repos, 901 planted bugs, 481 (53%) survived; 41 of 82 files under 50%; 26 files at 0%. $0, no model calls. Equivalent mutants not filtered (29% in an earlier hand-labelled set).

## Receipts

- [verify.md](https://github.com/acoyfellow/teeth/blob/main/receipts/verify.md): gate output and the A/B table recomputed from per-seat receipts
- [scan.md](https://github.com/acoyfellow/teeth/blob/main/receipts/scan.md): 58-repo scan
- [handcheck.md](https://github.com/acoyfellow/teeth/blob/main/receipts/handcheck.md): 2 misses checked by hand
- [refusal.md](https://github.com/acoyfellow/teeth/blob/main/receipts/refusal.md): a real Pi run, refused, tests written, then done
